_readme: THE REMAINING-WORK LEDGER, not a hiding place. Three properties keep it honest, and
1. every entry carries a one-line `reason`, an `owner_issue` and a `batch` — no entry
2. STALE ENTRIES FAIL THE SUITE, bidirectionally: an exempt cell that has acquired a
registered provoker (so it would now pass) fails and demands the entry be deleted,
and a `retained_legacy` condition no longer emitted anywhere fails the same way;
3. it prints its own size on every run, as the P2 metric.
A mirror grows silently; a ledger that fails when stale and prints its own count cannot.
`cells` exempts the TIER-B arc only (provoke -> follow the route -> arrive green). TIER A
— route resolution, verb existence, R4 discipline, payload validation — is armed for EVERY
cell and admits no exemptions at all.
THE CELL-KEYED WHY PINS ARE TIER A. The hint layer being ALIVE, the no-fabricated-fields
rule, hint/route agreement and cell closure are armed for every cell and CANNOT be exempted
here — the blanket `*` entry below does not reach them. A hint that throws used to degrade
silently to the caller's generic fallback, so an entire dead hint layer once read green
across 541 assertions; an exemption door on that pin would reopen exactly that hole.

cells.reason: Batch 1 lands the registry and typed routes only; the per-cell provoke->route->green fixtures are the later batches' work, one family per commit alongside its demotion

retained_legacy.reason: documents a REPRODUCED open/close view-split wedge; demoting lets an agent compose straight into it
demotion is coupled to the frontier-closure fix; alone it converts a loud freeze wall into a silent wedge
a failing aggregate with an empty canonical frontier loses the record of WHAT failed; [] vs [] reads as non-progress
deleting deriveLegacyClaimRoot removes a working capability for pre-#699 projects — an owner decision, not an implementer's
